title: Walter Barnes at the Arcadia and being drawn to Erskine Tate
summary: After Bernie Young he joins Walter Barnes; Erskine Tate wants him, so he swaps jobs with Barnes's bass player and learns string bass in two weeks.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Did you go with Erskine Tate after Bernie Young?
No. See, I went with Walter Barnes, at the Arcadia Ballroom on Broadway.
That's up north, here?
Up north, yeah, on Broadway.
Now, who was he?
Walter Barnes? What did Walter Barnes play? He was the band that got burn up in Natchez, Mississippi. You remember that?
No. When was that?

Well, I was still -- I was with Earl Hines, then. This was back in the thirties. They got trapped in a dance. I worked with him for a little while, and then Erskine Tate heard about me. And he wanted me to come with his band. So that's the reason I had to get on the bass fiddle. Because this was playing for silent pictures in the moving picture theater pit.
Now, with all the other bands you'd been playing tuba. And they had arrangements? It wasn't, you know, a "fake" band?
Oh, no, no. We had --
Everything was written.
Yeah, we had things written.
Okay, now. Tate was playing -- what theater was he playing at?
AT the Metropolitan Theater and the Vendome Theater.
Doubling?
Yeah.
But what did you do?

Well, during that time, that was during the time they was changing over from silent pictures to talkies, see. Like on Sundays they'd have talking pictures at the Metropolitan Theater, and then during the week they'd have silent pictures at the Vendome, so we'd go down and play
for the silent pictures in the Vendome Theater.
How big a band did Tate have?
Twelve pieces.
Twelve pieces. And that's when you switched to string bass?
That's when I switched to string bass.
Did you find that difficult?

No, I had about two weeks to learn it. Because back in them days we only gave two weeks notice. You didn't have to give a four weeks notice. So what we did, the bass player that was with Walter Barnes went with Erskine Tate, and I went with Erskine Tate. And -- no, Walter Barnes' bass player, we switched jobs.
I see. He was with --
He was with Walter Barnes. He went -- I went with Tate, and then he went with Walter Barnes. That's what it was.
What was his name?
I forgot.
He didn't like working with Tate?
No, we switched jobs because Tate wanted me. So we just changed jobs.
